title: Perseverance and Assurance
summary: Can a believer be sure of salvation? Can a true Christian fall away? The biblical teaching on assurance, warning passages and enduring to the end.
description: Many believers swing between false security and constant fear. This course studies God's promises to keep His people, the warning passages that call us to endure, the 'once saved, always saved' and 'conditional security' views held by different churches, the grounds of true assurance, and practical help for doubting and backsliding believers.
objectives: Explain the biblical promises of God's keeping power
Present fairly the eternal security and conditional security views
Explain the grounds of Christian assurance
Give pastoral help to doubters and backsliders
outcomes: Interpret Hebrews 6:4-6 and other warnings with care
Compare the Reformed, Baptist and Wesleyan-Holiness views
Counsel a doubting or backslidden believer from Scripture

modules.title: Kept by the Power of God
modules.intro: Scripture is full of promises that God keeps His people. This week we study them.

lessons.title: In the Father's hand
lessons.body:
Jesus said of His sheep, "I give unto them eternal life; and they shall never perish, neither shall any man pluck them out of my hand. My Father, which gave them me, is greater than all; and no man is able to pluck them out of my Father's hand" (John 10:28-29).

He also said, "him that cometh to me I will in no wise cast out... of all which he hath given me I should lose nothing" (John 6:37-39).

Eternal life is a present possession: "He that heareth my word, and believeth... hath everlasting life, and shall not come into condemnation" (John 5:24).

lessons.title: Nothing can separate us
lessons.body:
Paul ends Romans 8 with a triumphant list: "neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come, Nor height, nor depth, nor any other creature, shall be able to separate us from the love of God, which is in Christ Jesus our Lord" (8:38-39).

God's work is sure: "he which hath begun a good work in you will perform it until the day of Jesus Christ" (Philippians 1:6). Believers "are kept by the power of God through faith unto salvation" (1 Peter 1:5).

Note that God keeps us *through faith*. His power works by sustaining our trust in Him.

lessons.title: Christ's intercession and the Spirit's seal
lessons.body:
Believers are secure because Christ prays for them. To Peter He said, "I have prayed for thee, that thy faith fail not" (Luke 22:32). Peter fell badly but was restored. Christ "ever liveth to make intercession" and "is able also to save them to the uttermost" (Hebrews 7:25).

The Spirit is God's seal and pledge: "ye were sealed with that holy Spirit of promise, which is the earnest of our inheritance" (Ephesians 1:13-14), "sealed unto the day of redemption" (4:30).

God is "able to keep you from falling, and to present you faultless" (Jude 24).

terms.def: The teaching that true believers will continue in faith to the end.
God's work of keeping His people safe in salvation.
The life of God given to believers, possessed now and enjoyed for ever.
God's power guarding believers by sustaining their trust (1 Peter 1:5).
Completely and for ever; Christ saves to the uttermost (Hebrews 7:25).
The final day when believers' salvation is completed.

texts.teaches: Christ's sheep shall never perish and none can pluck them from His hand.
Nothing shall separate believers from the love of God in Christ.
God will complete the good work He began.
Believers are kept by the power of God through faith.
Jesus prayed that Peter's faith would not fail.

summary: Jesus promised that His sheep shall never perish.
Nothing outside can separate believers from God's love.
God keeps us through faith; His power sustains our trust.
Christ intercedes and the Spirit seals believers.

questions.q: According to John 10:28, Christ's sheep shall:
How does God keep believers, according to 1 Peter 1:5?
For whom did Jesus pray that his faith would not fail?
Which chapter ends with nothing separating us from God's love?

modules.title: The Warning Passages
modules.intro: Scripture also contains serious warnings against falling away. This week we read them carefully.

lessons.title: Hebrews 6 and 10
lessons.body:
Hebrews warns: "it is impossible for those who were once enlightened, and have tasted of the heavenly gift, and were made partakers of the Holy Ghost... If they shall fall away, to renew them again unto repentance" (6:4-6).

And: "if we sin wilfully after that we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more sacrifice for sins" (10:26).

The readers were Jewish Christians tempted to abandon Christ and return to the old sacrifices under persecution. The warnings concern deliberate, persistent rejection of Christ, not ordinary sins or struggles. The writer adds, "we are persuaded better things of you" (6:9).

lessons.title: Other warnings
lessons.body:
Other passages call believers to continue:

- "he that shall endure unto the end, the same shall be saved" (Matthew 24:13).
- Christ will present you holy "If ye continue in the faith grounded and settled" (Colossians 1:22-23).
- "If a man abide not in me, he is cast forth as a branch" (John 15:6).
- "Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall" (1 Corinthians 10:12).
- Some "concerning faith have made shipwreck" (1 Timothy 1:19).

These warnings are real and must not be explained away. They are one of the means God uses to keep His people watchful.

lessons.title: Those who went out from us
lessons.body:
Some who seemed to be believers do turn away. Judas was one of the Twelve. Demas "forsook" Paul, "having loved this present world" (2 Timothy 4:10).

John explains one way of understanding this: "They went out from us, but they were not of us; for if they had been of us, they would no doubt have continued with us" (1 John 2:19).

In the parable of the sower, some received the word with joy, "but have no root" and fell away in trial (Luke 8:13). Christians differ on whether such people were ever truly saved, as next week shows. All agree that lasting faith is the mark of the genuine.

terms.def: Deliberate abandonment of the Christian faith.
Turning from Christ, as warned in Hebrews 6:6.
In Hebrews 10:26, deliberate rejection of Christ after knowing the truth.
Continuing in faith through trials until death or Christ's return.
Paul's picture of those who abandoned faith and a good conscience (1 Timothy 1:19).
In the parable of the sower, those whose faith was shallow and temporary.

texts.teaches: Those who fall away cannot be renewed to repentance while they crucify Christ afresh.
Wilful sin after knowing the truth leaves no other sacrifice.
He that endures to the end shall be saved.
Let him that thinks he stands take heed lest he fall.
Those who left were not truly of us, or they would have continued.

summary: Hebrews warns against deliberately abandoning Christ.
Many texts call believers to continue and endure.
Some who seemed believers do turn away.
The warnings are real means God uses to keep believers watchful.

questions.q: Who were the first readers of Hebrews tempted to return to?
Who forsook Paul, having loved this present world?

options: He that endures to the end shall be saved

questions.q: What does 1 John 2:19 say about those who left?

modules.title: Two Views of Security
modules.intro: Christians understand the promises and warnings differently. This week we present the main views fairly.

lessons.title: Eternal security
lessons.body:
**Reformed** Christians teach the **perseverance of the saints**: all who are truly born again will persevere in faith to the end, because God keeps them. Those who fall away permanently were never truly regenerate (1 John 2:19). The warnings are God's means of ensuring perseverance.

Many **Baptists** hold a related view often called **eternal security** or "once saved, always saved". At its best this means a true believer cannot lose salvation, though he may fall into sin and be disciplined by God (Hebrews 12:6).

A danger is a careless version that says a person who 'prayed a prayer' is safe whatever they do afterwards. Scripture rejects this (Titus 1:16).

lessons.title: Conditional security
lessons.body:
**Wesleyan, Methodist, Holiness and many Pentecostal** Christians, including Deeper Life Bible Church, teach that a believer is secure while continuing in faith and obedience, but can by persistent, wilful sin and unbelief turn away and be lost.

They take the warnings at face value as describing real believers: "partakers of the Holy Ghost" (Hebrews 6:4), branches that were "in me" (John 15:2, 6). They stress that God's keeping is "through faith" (1 Peter 1:5), and faith can be abandoned.

They also teach that a backslider who returns in repentance will be received, as the father received the prodigal son (Luke 15:20-24).

lessons.title: Common ground
lessons.body:
Both views agree on vital truths:

1. Salvation is by grace through faith, not by works.
2. True faith perseveres and bears fruit.
3. A person living in persistent, unrepentant sin has no grounds for assurance (1 John 3:6-10).
4. The warnings must be taken seriously.
5. A struggling believer who comes to Christ in repentance will be received (1 John 1:9).

The practical difference is small: both call believers to "give diligence to make your calling and election sure" (2 Peter 1:10), and both call backsliders to return now.

terms.def: The view that a truly saved person cannot lose salvation.
A popular summary of eternal security, sometimes misused to excuse sin.
The view that believers are secure while continuing in faith, but can turn away and be lost.
Drifting or turning away from God after professing faith.
The son in Jesus' parable who wasted his inheritance and returned to a welcoming father.
Confirming one's calling through growth in godliness (2 Peter 1:10).

texts.teaches: Some profess to know God but deny Him in their works.
A branch that does not abide in Christ is cast forth and withers.
Beware of an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God.
Whoever is born of God does not continue in sin as a way of life.
Give diligence to make your calling and election sure.

summary: Reformed and many Baptists: true believers will persevere; they cannot be lost.
Wesleyan-Holiness, including Deeper Life: believers can turn away by persistent unbelief.
Careless 'once saved, always saved' teaching that excuses sin is unbiblical.
Both views call believers to diligence and backsliders to return.

questions.q: Which tradition teaches the perseverance of the saints?
Which church is an example of the conditional security view?
What do both views agree about persistent unrepentant sin?
options: It gives no grounds for assurance

questions.q: Which parable shows a father welcoming a returning son?

modules.title: Assurance and Restoration
modules.intro: God wants His children to know they are His. This week we study the grounds of assurance and how to help doubters and backsliders.

lessons.title: That ye may know
lessons.body:
John wrote his first letter "that ye may know that ye have eternal life" (1 John 5:13). Assurance is God's will for believers.

Assurance rests on three grounds:

1. **God's promises**: "He that hath the Son hath life" (5:12). This is the main ground.
2. **The Spirit's witness**: "The Spirit itself beareth witness with our spirit" (Romans 8:16).
3. **A changed life**: love for believers, obedience, and turning from sin (1 John 2:3; 3:14).

Assurance is not based on a past feeling or a single moment, but on a present trust in Christ.

lessons.title: Helping the doubting believer
lessons.body:
Sincere believers sometimes doubt because of sin, trials, depression, poor teaching or Satan's accusations (Revelation 12:10).

How to help:

- Point them to Christ and His promises, not to their feelings.
- Ask whether they are trusting Christ now; if so, John 6:37 is for them.
- Encourage confession of known sin (1 John 1:9).
- Remind them that weak faith is still faith: "Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief" (Mark 9:24).
- Encourage fellowship, prayer and the Lord's Supper.

Often the very concern to be right with God is a sign of the Spirit's work.

lessons.title: Restoring the backslider
lessons.body:
"Return, ye backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings" (Jeremiah 3:22). God's call to wanderers is full of grace.

Peter denied Jesus three times, yet Jesus restored him with three questions, "lovest thou me?" and recommissioned him (John 21:15-17). David sinned grievously, yet prayed, "Restore unto me the joy of thy salvation" (Psalm 51:12).

The church has a part: "if a man be overtaken in a fault, ye which are spiritual, restore such an one in the spirit of meekness" (Galatians 6:1). "He which converteth the sinner from the error of his way shall save a soul from death" (James 5:20).

terms.def: A believer's confidence that he truly belongs to Christ.
The Spirit's inner testimony that we are God's children (Romans 8:16).
Confidence of salvation without genuine faith or a changed life.
A name for Satan, who accuses believers before God (Revelation 12:10).
Bringing a fallen believer back to fellowship with God and the church.
Gentle humility in restoring others (Galatians 6:1).

texts.teaches: John wrote so believers may know they have eternal life.
He that has the Son has life.
Lord, I believe; help thou mine unbelief.
Return, backsliding children, and I will heal your backslidings.
Restore one overtaken in a fault in the spirit of meekness.

summary: God wants believers to know they have eternal life.
Assurance rests on God's promises, the Spirit's witness and a changed life.
Help doubters by pointing them to Christ, not their feelings.
God calls backsliders home; the church should restore them gently.

questions.q: Why did John write 1 John, according to 5:13?
options: That believers may know they have eternal life

questions.q: What is the main ground of assurance?
How many times did Jesus ask Peter 'lovest thou me?'
How should a fallen believer be restored?

short.q: What does John 10:28-29 teach about believers' security?
short.model: Christ gives His sheep eternal life; they shall never perish and no one can pluck them from His or the Father's hand.

short.q: Explain the setting and meaning of Hebrews 6:4-6.
short.model: Jewish Christians under persecution were tempted to abandon Christ for the old sacrifices; the warning is against deliberate, persistent rejection of Christ.

short.q: Summarise the Reformed view of perseverance.
short.model: All truly born-again believers will persevere because God keeps them; those who fall away permanently were never truly regenerate.
Held by Wesleyan, Holiness and many Pentecostal churches: believers are secure while continuing in faith but can turn away by persistent unbelief and be lost.

short.q: Name the three grounds of assurance.
short.model: God's promises, the Spirit's witness and the evidence of a changed life.

short.q: How would you help a doubting believer?
short.model: Point them to Christ's promises rather than feelings, encourage confession of sin, assure them that weak faith is faith, and encourage fellowship and prayer.

lists.q: List four promises or texts of God's keeping power.
List three warning passages about falling away.
List four common causes of doubt in believers.

assignments.title: Promises and warnings
assignments.prompt: Choose two promise passages and two warning passages from the course. Explain each in its context. Then show how the Reformed and Wesleyan-Holiness traditions hold them together, and what both views require of believers today.

assignments.title: A letter to a backslider
assignments.prompt: Write a pastoral letter to a friend who once followed Christ but has drifted away. Use at least five passages from the course to call them back with both seriousness and hope.

reading: D. A. Carson, Reflections on Assurance (essay)
J. Matthew Pinson (ed.), Four Views on Eternal Security
Thomas Brooks, Heaven on Earth: A Treatise on Christian Assurance
